bra-size-calculator.assumptionNote: This calculator gives a starting size. Brands fit differently, so always check the fit: the band should be snug on the loosest hook and the centre gore should sit flat.
benefits: A correct band size carries about 80% of the support, not the straps.
Takes two minutes at home with a soft tape measure.
Gives you a confident starting size before ordering online.
Explains sister sizes so you can adjust between brands.

faqs.a: Band: around your ribcage directly under the bust, snug, after a normal exhale. Bust: around the fullest part of the bust, wearing a light non-padded bra, tape level all the way round.
faqs.q: How do I take the two measurements?

faqs.a: Sister sizes keep the same cup volume on a different band: go up one band and down one cup (34C = 36B = 32D). Useful when your exact size is out of stock.
Most adults change band or cup within a few years of weight change, pregnancy or aging. If the band rides up or the cups gap or spill, re-measure.
Straps digging in usually means the band is too loose, so the straps are doing the band's job. A snugger band fixes most strap problems.
faqs.q: Why do my straps dig in?

faqs.a: The band should sit level, snug on the loosest hook, and the centre gore should lie flat against your chest. Spillage over the cups means the cup is too small.
faqs.q: How do I know the fit is right?

faqs.a: UK and US sizing mostly match up to DD, then diverge (UK uses FF, G, GG while the US uses DDD/F, G). EU sizing uses centimetre-based bands. Always check the brand's chart.
faqs.q: Do UK, US and EU sizes match?

bra-size-calculator.formula:
Band = underbust rounded to the nearest even inch.
Cup = bust minus band, in inches: 1 = A, 2 = B, 3 = C, 4 = D, 5 = DD/E, 6 = DDD/F, 7 = G.
Bra size = band + cup letter (for example 34C).
howTo: Measure your bust at its fullest point with a soft tape, wearing a light non-padded bra.
Measure your underbust snugly around the ribcage, right under the bust.
Enter both measurements; your band, cup and full bra size appear instantly.
Try the size on and use the fit check in the FAQ if anything feels off.
keyFacts: A bra size has two parts: the band number (ribcage) and the cup letter (bust minus band).
About 80% of breast support should come from the band, not the straps.
Cup letters are relative: a 34D cup is smaller in volume than a 38D cup.
The band is rounded to the nearest even inch in the standard US/UK method.
Around 70-80% of women wear the wrong bra size, most often a band that is too loose.
Sister sizes (for example 34C, 36B, 32D) hold the same cup volume on different bands.

bra-size-calculator.quickAnswer: Bra size comes from two measurements: the underbust gives the band, and bust minus band gives the cup. A 36-inch bust with a 31.5-inch underbust rounds to a 32 band, and the 4-inch difference is a D cup - size 32D. The band should do about 80% of the support work, not the straps.
bra-size-calculator.tagline: Find your band size, cup size and full bra size from two simple measurements.
bra-size-calculator.workedExample:
Bust 36 in, underbust 31.5 in:
1. Band: 31.5 rounds to the nearest even number = 32.
2. Difference: 36 - 32 = 4 inches.
3. Cup scale: 1 = A, 2 = B, 3 = C, 4 = D.
4. Bra size = 32D.
Sister sizes with the same cup volume: 34C and 36B.
